ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening on each UBO, director, shareholder, signatory and beneficial owner chain shall be conducted before acceptance against (1) PBOC beneficial owner register and PEP lists, (2) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (3) OFAC SDN/SSI and country/entity lists, (4) China Ministry of Public Security and military sanction lists, (5) China MOFCOM unreliable entity list, and (6) Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission and FATF public statements. Such screening must be repeated within 24 hours before signing, use robust fuzzy matching, and include adverse media and source-of-wealth checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Registration System (integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the China Integrated Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE statutory name must be in Chinese and follow the four-tier naming convention: administrative division + trade name + industry or operating characteristics + enterprise legal form (limited liability company). Pinyin/English transliteration is supplementary and does not replace the Chinese statutory name; an English name may be recorded separately in the articles of association or supplemental registration, but no English-only statutory name is permitted. The trade name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name in the same industry and administrative region, and any foreign-invested trade name must be capable of phonetic transliteration into Chinese characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of receiving a written or electronic rejection from the SAMR name registration system, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the SAMR at the next higher level or with the competent people's government at the same level. The application must state the grounds of distinctiveness, include the intended business scope and evidence of non-conflict, and may be submitted through the same online portal. If the reconsideration decision is unfavorable, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. A fresh name reservation may also be filed immediately with a corrected proposed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox permissibility is rejected for this ISIC 5630 specialty tea salon business. A WFOE must maintain a physical registered domicile that is also its principal place of business. Local Market Supervision Administration authorities require a food business permit tied to an actual operating address; State Taxation Administration authorities require physical presence for VAT invoice administration, tax UKey activation, and e-invoice registration; and PBOC-regulated banks require an on-site compliance visit before opening a basic deposit account under AML/CFT requirements and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3. A virtual office or commercial mailbox cannot satisfy these statutory, food-safety, tax, or bank due-diligence thresholds.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 75 percent risk for a food-and-beverage service entity. The checklist includes: physical signage matching the registered name; lease agreement or ownership proof; food business license; fire safety and sanitary inspection certificates; VAT invoice and POS transaction records; tea inventory and supplier sourcing documents; employee social insurance and payroll records; bank settlement statements; and UBO information filings. Unannounced joint inspections by local SAMR, fire authorities, and tax officials are common for tea salons.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (公司法), Articles 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 17-1, 18, 98, 101, 108, 113, 128, 154, 172 and 387; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例), Articles 7-11; Food Safety and Sanitation Act (食品安全衛生管理法), Article 8; Business Registration Act (商業登記法), applicable provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; online company registration portal administered by MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司登記申請書), Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), and Foreign Investment Approval Letter (投資審定函).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Taiwan Company Act; however, issued shares must be fully subscribed and the approved foreign investment capital must be actually remitted and deposited into a Taiwan bank account in the company name, verified by a licensed CPA before registration filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned incorporate Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise Ltd. (WFOE) under the Companies Act of Taiwan, and subscribe to 100% of the company's initially issued shares as capital; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be established at [registered address], and the registered address is approved for Food and Beverage Service Business Registration; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Chairman and General Manager, [Name] as Finance Officer/Auditor, with exclusive authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and make filings; FURTHER RESOLVED, that all corporate documentation, including Articles of Incorporation, foreign investment approval application, and business permits, be executed and submitted; ALL SUBJECT TO shareholder approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval from the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - Online Foreign Investment Screening System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment application by the sole foreign shareholder, including the investor qualification documents, capital remittance plan, proposed capital amount, business scope, and a local representative appointment. The Investment Commission reviews the application under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and issues the Foreign Investment Approval Letter (投資審定函) upon approval.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form
Investor incorporation certificate and articles of incorporation (notarized and certified)
Audited financial statements or bank reference of the foreign investor
Power of attorney appointing local formation agent or legal representative
Proposed business plan for specialty tea salon lounge
Shareholder list and capital remittance schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency notice, submit the missing business plan and source-of-funds evidence within 14 days. If approval is denied, file a written reconsideration within 30 days or revise the investment amount and business scope and reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Pre-approve Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the MOEA online name reservation system and submit the proposed Chinese company name with the selected business scope codes, including F501030 (飲料店業, beverage store) for the specialty tea salon and, if light meals are served, F501060 (餐館業, restaurant service). Obtain the name pre-approval certificate required for subsequent filing.
required_dossiers: Company name pre-approval application
Proposed Chinese company name
Business scope code list (F501030 / F501060)
Applicant identity or agent authorization letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or conflict, submit up to three alternative Chinese names and reapply. If business scope codes are deemed incompatible, consult MOEA service desk to revise the scope description to cover specialty loose-leaf tea service and lounge operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Temporary Bank Account and Verify Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in Taiwan; accredited Taiwan CPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Foreign Investment Approval is obtained, open a temporary or new-company bank account in the intended WFOE name. Remit the approved paid-in capital in NT$, obtain the bank deposit certificate, and engage a Taiwan CPA to issue the capital verification report evidencing that the subscription price has been fully paid.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment approval letter
Company name pre-approval certificate
Draft articles of incorporation
Passport, ARC, or ID of the legal representative or authorized signatory
Bank account opening application and KYC forms
Remittance advice or bank credit confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional authority evidence, provide the draft board resolution and Foreign Investment Approval Letter. If capital is delayed, obtain a bank remittance tracer and apply to the Investment Commission for an extension of the remittance period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Notarized Articles of Incorporation and Shareholder/Board Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan civil notary or District Court Notary Office; licensed CPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Chinese-language Articles of Incorporation, including company name, business scope, authorized capital, share structure, director appointments, registered office, and internal governance rules. Execute the sole shareholder resolution and the first board resolution, then notarize the signatures if required by the bank or company registrar.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Chinese
Shareholder meeting minutes approving the incorporation
Board meeting minutes or board consent approving share subscription
List of initial directors/officers and consent-to-serve forms
CPA capital verification report
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies, correct the Chinese translation, identification numbers, share amounts, and registered office details and re-notarize. If the capital verification report is deficient, instruct the CPA to supplement the source-of-funds evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Registration with MOEA and Obtain Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Online Company Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed company registration application to MOEA, attaching the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital verification report, registered office proof, and consent forms for directors. Pay the statutory registration fee and receive the company registration number and incorporation certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for company registration (公司登記申請書)
Foreign investment approval certificate
Articles of Incorporation
CPA capital verification report
Registered office lease or ownership certificate
Consent forms and identification of directors/officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a deficiency notice, correct and resubmit within 15 days. If registration is rejected, file an administrative reconsideration to MOEA within 30 days or re-file after curing the stated defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, Uniform Invoices and Withholding Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) - local tax administration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for tax registration to obtain the tax identification number (統一編號), register for business tax (VAT), uniform invoice usage, employees' income tax withholding, and periodic filing obligations. Complete the tax registration before ordering or issuing uniform invoices.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Company seal and responsible person identity documents
Seal certificate (印鑑證明)
Operational address proof and lease agreement
Foreign investment approval certificate
Application form for tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the registered address, provide the building use permit and landlord consent. If uniform invoice issuance approval is delayed, apply for provisional manual invoice authorization and amend the tax registration accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Food Enterprise Registration, Building and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) through local Health Bureau; Taipei City or municipal Department of Economic Development; local Fire Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Food Enterprise Registration (食品業者登錄) in the FDA non-denial electronic declaration system, submit sanitation self-inspection data, employee health check records, and floor plans. Obtain the building occupancy/use license verification and fire safety certification from the local Fire Bureau prior to operation.
required_dossiers: Food enterprise registration application
Building use license or occupancy certificate and floor plan
Fire safety equipment inspection certificate or checklist
Employee health examination records and food hygiene training certificates
Registered lease contract or ownership proof
Company registration and tax registration certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection is non-compliant, install the required extinguishers, alarms, evacuation signage, and emergency lighting, then request re-inspection. If the health bureau queries food handler records, submit valid medical examination certificates within 7 days. If the building use license is incompatible, apply for a use license amendment or relocate the salon.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Labor Registration, Occupational Safety and Operational Launch Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bureau of Labor Insurance; local Department of Labor/Occupational Safety Division; Taipei City Labor Affairs Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a labor insurance employer, enroll all employees in labor insurance, national health insurance, and pension contributions, and submit workplace safety and health rules under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Obtain the final civil defense, fire safety, and workplace clearance before opening to the public.
required_dossiers: Labor insurance and health insurance enrollment forms
Employee payroll and employment contracts
Fire evacuation plan and building fire-safety approval
Occupational safety and health management plan
Business tax registration and company registration certificates
Public liability insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If labor insurance registration is rejected due to incomplete data, submit corrected employee identification and employer seal documents within 10 days. If occupational safety clearance requires further inspection, arrange a workplace safety inspection and remedy any citations before reopening.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Economic Development, Taipei City Government or applicable local municipal government, in coordination with Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food and Beverage Service Business Registration Certificate (食品業者登錄字號) and Business Premises Use License (建築物使用執照/場所營運許可) for the specialty tea salon lounge.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOENV), Taiwan; local Municipal Environmental Protection Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Low-Risk Registration/Exemption: full EIA is not required for a small-scale beverage service with floor area below 1,000 m2 and daily wastewater discharge under 50 m3. The operation must complete environmental self-declaration and obtain a general wastewater discharge permit if discharging to public sewers. If tea roasting, charcoal heating or gas combustion equipment is introduced, additional air pollution operating permit review will be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent must meet Taiwan water pollution effluent standards: pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, SS ≤ 30 mg/L, and oil/grease ≤ 10 mg/L if discharged to surface waters; for public sewer discharge, install and maintain grease traps and comply with local sewer discharge ordinances. For air emissions, all tea processing and kitchen cooking exhaust must be captured by a fume extraction system with grease filters; regulated VOC/NMHC emissions shall remain below 0.4 kg/hr, and odor control at the property boundary shall comply with local air pollution control standards. Solid waste, including spent tea leaves and food residue, shall be separated, stored in covered containers, and removed by licensed waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, the WFOE must obtain: (1) Fire Services Act safety equipment inspection certification, including fire extinguishers, alarms, and evacuation signage; (2) building occupancy/use license verification confirming structural load, ceiling height, exit capacity, and public assembly safety; (3) occupational safety and health workplace clearance covering electrical, kitchen, and slip hazards; (4) food handler health certificates and sanitation training completion; and (5) public liability insurance and monitored fire alarm/security systems as required by the local fire department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) – Tax Administration; official portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw; local filing with the regional National Taxation Bureau.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Obtain foreign investment approval and company incorporation via the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA). 2. Apply to the regional National Taxation Bureau using the MOEA-issued articles of incorporation and registration certificate. 3. Obtain an 8-digit Unified Business Number (UBN), which serves as both the TIN and VAT registration code. 4. Download the electronic tax registration certificate from the Tax E-Government portal. 5. Register for the Electronic Uniform Invoice (EUI) platform if VAT-registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Taiwan's Income Tax Act. All limited companies are taxed at the entity level. A small-scale enterprise may be taxed under a deemed assessment regime if monthly sales remain below the VAT registration threshold, but such treatment is mandated by turnover and not an elective classification. No pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$200,000 average monthly sales; businesses below this may be classified as small-scale taxpayers without mandatory invoice issuance, but VAT registration is required once any one month exceeds the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic Uniform Invoicing (EUI) is mandatory for all VAT-registered enterprises. B2B invoices must be uploaded to the MOF E-Invoice Platform within 48 hours of issuance; B2C invoices must be uploaded within 7 days. Integration uses certified API service providers; no real-time transactional fiscal stamping is required, but each invoice must bear a government-allocated serial number and be traceable in the platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (i) physical export of goods where the goods leave Taiwan under a customs export declaration, including cross-border e-commerce sales of loose-leaf tea; and (ii) taxable services rendered to foreign enterprises or used entirely overseas, supported by invoices issued in foreign currency and remittance evidence. Pure in-person salon services provided to tourists inside Taiwan are domestic supplies and remain subject to 5% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Form 出口報單)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice (E-Invoice) with 0% tax code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are cross-verified against customs export records, foreign exchange settlement data, and the e-invoice platform. Excessive or fraudulent claims trigger immediate VAT and business income tax reassessments, interest charges, and penalties of 1.5 to 5 times the underpaid tax under Business Tax Act Article 51. Criminal fraud penalties under the Tax Collection Act include imprisonment and fines. Refund clawbacks are retrospectively applied within the 7-year statutory limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), the central bank, is the supreme monetary authority; the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), administratively managed by PBOC, is the designated authority for exchange control, current- and capital-account surveillance, and the trade-monitoring system. The National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA) supervises banks and payment institutions on licensing, KYC, and anti-money-laundering enforcement jointly with PBOC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible for current-account items, including cross-border trade in tea goods, salon services, dividends and royalties, provided the remitting bank verifies the real-transaction background and reports the transaction to SAFE. Capital-account items remain regulated. A WFOE receiving equity capital must complete the AMR Foreign Investment Information Report and obtain a SAFE capital-project registration through its designated bank before the Taiwan investor can fund the FDI capital account. Profit-remittance hurdles include the annual statutory audit, allocation of the 10% statutory surplus reserve until that reserve equals 50% of registered capital, payment of enterprise income tax, and a board resolution approving the dividend. Dividend withholding for a Taiwan corporate shareholder is 10% absent a ratified cross-strait tax arrangement, and only decreases if the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement is implemented by the tax authorities of both sides.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China's mandatory export-proceeds surrender regime was repealed in 2012; no statutory conversion ratio or surrender timeline currently applies. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in a foreign-exchange settlement account or settled into RMB voluntarily. Nevertheless, proceeds must be repatriated to China within the credit terms of the underlying export contract, and a deferred-collection report is mandatory where payment is not expected within 90 days of the customs export declaration. SAFE's monitoring system assigns A-class, B-class and C-class status; B- and C-class enterprises lose the fast-track verification and voluntary-settlement options.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Information Filing (Company Law Article 22-1) – online declaration of directors, supervisors, managers, major shareholders, and shareholding ratios
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Department of Commerce) via the Company Registration and Management Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 31 March; data as at 31 December of the prior year must be reported
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or knowingly false filing triggers a fine of NTD 50,000–500,000 (approximately USD 1,600–16,000) imposed on the responsible person; each successive non-compliant period may be punished repeatedly; no administrative strike-off applies for this filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (annual tax declaration for the previous fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau under the Ministry of Finance (local jurisdictional office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 May to 31 May; covers the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a surcharge of 1% of unpaid tax for every two days, capped at 15%; failure to file is subject to a fine up to NTD 30,000; fraudulent underreporting may lead to criminal liability and freezing of assets. No administrative strike-off, but tax liens may be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and approval of financial statements (shareholder meeting resolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing required; minutes and financial statements must be retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by 30 June for calendar-year companies; shareholders must be notified at least 15 days in advance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate monetary penalty attaches for non-holding; however, financial statements cannot be legally approved for profit distribution, and the responsible person may be subject to sanctions under the Company Law for serious non-compliance; no administrative strike-off applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory certified audit applies to a company whose paid-in capital exceeds NTD 30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000), or to companies undertaking public issuance; specialty tea salon WFOEs below this threshold are not statutorily required to have audited financial statements but may elect to do so for banking or investor purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: TIFRS (Taiwan-adapted IFRS) for public companies; private WFOE entities generally apply the Taiwan Business Enterprise Accounting Standards (BEAS) and related financial accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Law Article 22-1, every company must annually confirm and file, during 1 January–31 March, the particulars of directors, supervisors, managers, and all shareholders holding more than 10% of the outstanding shares, including national IDs and exact shareholding ratios; any shareholding transfers occurring during the year are reflected in the next annual filing, and there is no separate transfer-triggered filing obligation in the ordinary course.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax rate; plus a 5% retained earnings surcharge on undistributed surplus where applicable and a 12% minimum tax under the Income Basic Tax Act for most profit-seeking enterprises.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific tax holiday applies to specialty tea salons. Available incentives include the 20% research and development expense deduction, investment tax credits for qualifying automation and green assets, and the small-profit enterprise exemption or simplified rate only where statutory thresholds are satisfied. The effective tax rate for a standard WFOE tea salon remains close to the 20% headline rate once AMT and retained earnings surcharges are considered.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書), filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance Tax e-Filing Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return; provisional tax payment return for the first half-year filed by 30 September, with an optional second provisional return by 31 January.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed between 1 May and 31 May of the year following the close of the fiscal year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, the return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, service revenue and other business receipts from high-end loose-leaf tea, cultural ceramic salon admission and retail sales, stated net of VAT, returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taiwan-source revenue of the WFOE must be fully included; a non-resident head office or shareholder cannot exclude revenue earned through the Taiwan establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct service costs, including premium tea leaves, hand-made ceramic wares, salon consumables, direct labor and properly allocated overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Purchases from a non-resident related supplier must be supported by contemporaneous arm's length analysis; the deduction will be denied if transfer pricing documentation thresholds apply and are not met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after book-tax adjustments, including transfer pricing adjustments, disallowed expenses, loss carryforward utilization and permanent differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office allocations, non-resident director fees and cross-border management charges are deductible only when directly traceable to Taiwan-source income and supported by contracts, invoices and local substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 20% on taxable income before foreign tax credits, investment tax credits and alternative minimum tax, after applying Article 39 loss carryforward deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only with verified foreign tax evidence; a non-resident shareholder cannot claim a credit for Taiwan withholding tax on dividends as a deduction of the WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 3% surcharge on the unpaid tax for each two-week delinquency period, capped at 15%, plus daily arrears interest from the statutory due date. Deliberate non-filing or false filing may result in an estimated assessment and a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on gross dividends paid to a non-resident profit-seeking enterprise or non-resident individual shareholder; resident shareholders are not subject to dividend withholding but the undistributed earnings surcharge of 5% may apply at corporate level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident mainland China shareholder must obtain a Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) from the State Taxation Administration, complete a beneficial ownership statement, provide the shareholding register and the WFOE board dividend resolution, and submit these to the Taiwan withholding agent. The withholding agent files the non-resident tax exemption or rate-reduction application with the competent National Taxation Bureau before or at the time of distribution; if treaty relief is not granted at source, the non-resident must file a refund claim within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis withholding tax is 20% for royalties and 20% for interest paid to a non-resident without a Taiwan permanent establishment. Under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement, eligible mainland Chinese beneficial owners may obtain reduced rates, commonly 7% for royalties and 10% for interest, while qualifying dividend payments may be reduced to 10%, or 5% where the mainland shareholder has held 25% or more of the WFOE for at least 12 months.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$200 million in aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Local File; NT$300 million triggers a Master File; country-by-country reporting applies when group consolidated revenue exceeds NT$27 billion. Even below these thresholds, the WFOE must maintain a transfer pricing study if the tax authority issues a documentation notice.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not apply a GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but anti-avoidance is enforced through the substance-over-form doctrine under the Tax Collection Act and the general anti-avoidance provisions of the Income Basic Tax Act. The specialty tea salon WFOE must maintain real local staff, physical tea and ceramic inventory, local pricing discretion, board minutes, contractual risk and bank accounts to avoid being recharacterized as a shell or nominee of the mainland shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or Fictitious Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of point-of-sale and credit-card tea salon revenue, use of counterfeit uniform invoices, creation of fictitious rent, décor or supplier expenses, and diversion of cash proceeds into private accounts to reduce the WFOE taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Collection Act, fraudulent evasion may result in criminal imprisonment of up to five years, criminal fines, a penal surcharge of one to three times the underpaid tax, and deemed assessment where books and records are unavailable or unreliable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false invoices, suppress cash sales or direct deceptive bookkeeping are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties. The tax authority may freeze bank accounts, seize assets, restrict travel against the legal representative, and criminal conviction may result in director disqualification and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mispricing premium tea-leaf imports or cultural ceramics purchased from a mainland affiliate, paying unsubstantiated royalties or management fees to offshore group companies, or using excessive shareholder debt to erode Taiwan taxable profits without formal transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recharacterize intercompany transactions under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act, impose deemed arm's length income, deny deductions for undocumented related-party charges, and assess a transfer pricing penalty surcharge of up to 1.5 times the additional tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve knowingly false transfer pricing documentation or direct the filing of falsified comparability analyses can be held civilly liable in shareholder or creditor actions. In aggravated cases, the corporate veil is pierced, exposing beneficial owners to restitutionary liability, travel restrictions and criminal prosecution for fraudulent declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of the tea-salon WFOE as an invoicing shell for routing funds, use of artificial tea-ceremony consulting fees to shift value offshore, or reliance on nominee directors with no local decision-making, physical presence or genuine operational risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The competent authority may deny treaty benefits and reimpose the full 21% dividend withholding and 20% royalty withholding rates, assess the 12% alternative minimum tax on overstated no-tax profits, and refer suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit for money-laundering investigation under the Money Laundering Control Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate form is abused, courts may disregard limited liability and hold shareholders and directors personally responsible for corporate tax debts and AML penalties. Legal representatives may face travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment for reckless false declarations designed to conceal the true beneficial ownership structure.
